holder: David Strouse; William B. Wilson; operators including David Homer Bates
dates_as_supported: April arrival; Strouse appointment footnote15 May1861; Wilson manager during21 July in Bates
evidence: Bates describes instruments in Sanderson room, orders direct from Secretary of War, personally delivering Ellsworth news to Lincoln24 May, and Lincoln waiting in office21 July.
disposition: IN-WINDOW OFFICE; presidential hold/trim authority not established
needed: Dated incoming routing/screening order and holder tenure. No conclusion that nobody ever screened an early telegram.

office: Headquarters of the Army; War Department confirmation
evidence: Scott requires Commanding General permission for army-operation dispatches; Cameron confirms.
disposition: IN-WINDOW SECURITY ORDER; not proof of holding Lincoln incoming copies
needed: Scope of execution, incoming presidential path and dated responsible operator. Do not recast public transmission censorship as a universal presidential filter.

dates_as_supported: Hay1866 recollection of administration generally; no dated March-July handover
evidence: Hay says he opened/read/answered letters and selected newspaper items; Nicolay handled visitors, messages to Congress and general supervision; delegation grew gradually.
disposition: MAIL SCREENING ATTESTED; activation/tenure within target window held
needed: Dated in-window duty record. General retrospective account cannot establish a5 March start or authority over every military wire.

holder: Thomas T. Eckert; commanding general George B. McClellan; Cameron instructions
dates_as_supported: September context; specific withholding21 October1861; order issue date unknown
evidence: Military telegrams to general first; Stone dispatch withheld from Lincoln until he saw it in McClellan room.
disposition: OUTSIDE WINDOW; cannot backdate to July
needed: Original appointment/order dates if later-window work proceeds. October incident does not establish an absence before October.

office: War Department telegraph office after centralization
dates_as_supported: March1862 office move after Monitor-Merrimac fight, in Bates
evidence: Bates dates final move beside Stanton office to1862.

holder: L. P. Walker; Major Tyler; J. B. Jones
dates_as_supported: Jones installation diary19 May1861; June and July continuity observations, not full legal tenure
evidence: Jones opens/reads letters and abstracts contents on backs; Walker marks replies; Tyler and Jones draft them. June4 describes workload. July11 and13 describe office processing.
disposition: IN-WINDOW DEPARTMENTAL SCREENING; before Davis first sight not established
needed: Routing showing these papers reached Davis only through this office. His22 June entry instead describes Davis seeking a letter he had already referred to Walker (p54). Do not create a universal wire filter.

holder: A. T. Bledsoe; L. P. Walker
dates_as_supported: 15 July1861 acting order described; Walker returned evening16 July; not full legal tenure
evidence: Jones records President order for Bledsoe to act during Walker absence; separate from Jones existing mail work.
disposition: IN-WINDOW ACTING OFFICE; presidential interception not established
needed: Actual order and correspondence routing. No personal dispositions inferred from Jones criticism.

holder: F. W. Pickens; G. T. Beauregard
dates_as_supported: 9 April1861 seized official Sumter outgoing mail
evidence: Private letters forwarded, official packages retained and sent to Confederate government; Hayne trusted to carry important dispatches.
disposition: IN-WINDOW INTERCEPTION; enemy mail, not Davis ordinary inbox
needed: Do not use this military isolation of enemy fort as a civilian presidential filter post.

evidence: Requested personal presidential delivery changed to transmission through General-in-Chief; paper was transmitted to President.
disposition: SCOPED IN-WINDOW FORWARDING; no documented hold/trim
needed: Separate evidence of discretionary screening before applying general filter role. Conveyance alone is not resistance.

dates_as_supported: 1861 volume index points to appointment p55 and endorsement p330; underlying pages not retrieved
evidence: Rice University index supplies retrieval locators; it does not disclose duties or the dated endorsement text.
pages: index entry Josselyn; UNREAD underlying pp55,330
disposition: HOLD; no historical duty or date inferred
needed: Read Papers of Jefferson Davis vol7 pp55,330 and the underlying documents. No claim about Harrison1862 from search snippets.

holder: William H. Seward; unnamed Assistant Secretary receives request
dates_as_supported: 13 March1861 receipt;15 March memorandum;8 April direction for external delivery
evidence: Assistant Secretary receives Banks sealed communication intended for Secretary; Seward memorandum describes request and says he submitted his paper to President, who sanctioned decision. External delivery was delayed with commissioners consent.
disposition: IN-WINDOW SCOPED DIPLOMATIC SCREENING AND SUMMARY; not general incoming-wire filter
needed: No blanket role or resistant hold. Exact date President saw each original letter is unknown. Do not turn agreed delay to commissioners into a delay of news to Lincoln.
